s: W&P, Letter 1

q: In very truth, I cannot think it is your grace, but the madness of others, that sows such seed.
s: W&P, Letter 1

q: What poor priest will dare to attack crimes or to inveigh against vices?
s: W&P, Letter 1

q: I would write at greater length; but I am hindered by the toils of preaching.
s: W&P, Letter 1

q: You have loved Him above all others, and that in truth most wisely.
s: W&P, Letter 2

q: He never breaketh His troth; neither indeed can He.
s: W&P, Letter 2

q: Ponder this well, dear brides of Christ the glorious King.
s: W&P, Letter 2

s: W&P, Letter 4

s: W&P, Letter 4

s: W&P, Letter 5

q: Study to avenge rather the wrongs done to God than those done to yourselves.
s: W&P, Letter 5

s: W&P, Letter 5

s: W&P, Letter 5

s: W&P, Letter 8

s: W&P, Letter 8

q: Such was the first origin of the accusation laid against me, and of all my troubles.

q: I am innocent of the things of which my adversaries accuse me; and of this I call to witness our Lord Jesus Christ.
s: M, First Series, Letter I, to the College of Cardinals

q: I burn with an ardent zeal for the gospel; and my soul is sad, for I know not what to resolve on.
s: M, First Series, Letter III

q: May peace be with you, that peace that is not given with the world, with the flesh, and the devil.
s: M, First Series, Letter III

q: What, indeed, are the riches of the world to me?
s: M, First Series, Letter IV, to the Rector of the University of Prague

q: What affliction can their loss cause me?
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: And, lastly, what is death, if this miserable life be torn from me?
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: He who loses it in this world triumphs even over death, and finds true life in the next.
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: But men, blinded by luxury, vainglory, and ambition, understand not these things.
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: Woe, then, unto me if I preach not against such an abomination!
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: Woe unto me if I weep not, if I write not against it!
s: M, First Series, Letter IV

q: Have full confidence; for Christ has overcome, and you will overcome also.
s: M, First Series, Letter VI, to the believers in Prague

s: M, First Series, Letter VI

q: But I feel a firm confidence that God will not permit them to succeed.
s: M, First Series, Letter VI

q: If, then, God, the most powerful and just of defenders, is with us, what evil work can prevail against us?
s: M, First Series, Letter VI

q: What fear, what death, can separate us from Him?
s: M, First Series, Letter VI

q: I myself only live by his mercy and grace.
s: M, First Series, Letter VII

q: I have faith in my Saviour, and I feel confident that all things will happen, both to you and to me, for our good.
s: M, First Series, Letter IX

q: In doing such things, it is against themselves that they labour; and it is they who ought to tremble.
s: M, First Series, Letter IX

q: Strengthen your hearts, dearly beloved, for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ is nigh.
s: M, Letter X

s: M, Letter X

s: M, Letter X

q: Be assured, that whatever God may have determined in relation to me, his will shall be done…
s: M, Letter XI

q: Woe, then, to such priests as neglect the word of God!
s: M, Letter XI

q: Woe to them who prevent the word of God from being preached and listened to!
s: M, Letter XI

q: Rejoice, for the Lord of the universe lay poor in a stable, in order that our poverty might be changed into riches.
s: M, Letter XII

q: Rejoice, dearly-beloved, that the predictions of the prophets and of the saints have been fulfilled.
s: M, Letter XII

q: Let it be our most earnest study, therefore, to dwell upon the life of Jesus Christ.
s: Book I, ch. 1

q: Vanity of vanities, all is vanity, save to love God, and Him only to serve.
s: Book I, ch. 1

q: I had rather feel contrition than be skilful in the definition thereof.
s: Book I, ch. 1

q: He who knoweth himself well is vile in his own sight; neither regardeth he the praises of men.
s: Book I, ch. 2

q: Be not high-minded, but rather confess thine ignorance.
s: Book I, ch. 2

q: All of us are weak and frail; hold thou no man more frail than thyself.
s: Book I, ch. 2

q: Our own judgment and feelings often deceive us, and we discern but little of the truth.
s: Book I, ch. 3

q: O God, who art the Truth, make me one with Thee in everlasting love.
s: Book I, ch. 3

q: This is great wisdom, not to be hasty in action, or stubborn in our own opinions.
s: Book I, ch. 4

q: Ask not, who hath said this or that, but look to what he says.
s: Book I, ch. 5

q: Men pass away, but the truth of the Lord endureth for ever.
s: Book I, ch. 5

q: Whensoever a man desireth aught above measure, immediately he becometh restless.
s: Book I, ch. 6

q: For true peace of heart is to be found in resisting passion, not in yielding to it.
s: Book I, ch. 6

q: Rest not upon thyself, but build thy hope in God.
s: Book I, ch. 7

q: Peace is ever with the humble man, but in the heart of the proud there is envy and continual wrath.
s: Book I, ch. 7

q: Open not thine heart to every man, but deal with one who is wise and feareth God.
s: Book I, ch. 8

q: Far safer is it to live in subjection than in a place of authority.
s: Book I, ch. 9

q: Many a time I wish that I had held my peace, and had not gone amongst men.
s: Book I, ch. 10

q: Blessed are the single-hearted, for they shall have abundance of peace.
s: Book I, ch. 11

q: If each year should see one fault rooted out from us, we should go quickly on to perfection.
s: Book I, ch. 11

q: As fire testeth iron, so doth temptation the upright man.
s: Book I, ch. 13

q: Oftentimes we know not what strength we have; but temptation revealeth to us what we are.
s: Book I, ch. 13

q: Look well unto thyself, and beware that thou judge not the doings of others.
s: Book I, ch. 14

q: He doth much who loveth much.
s: Book I, ch. 15

q: We are ready to see others made perfect, and yet we do not amend our own shortcomings.
s: Book I, ch. 16

q: Thou art called to endure and to labour, not to a life of ease and trifling talk.
s: Book I, ch. 17

q: They were strangers to the world, but unto God they were as kinsmen and friends.
s: Book I, ch. 18

q: No man safely talketh but he who loveth to hold his peace.
s: Book I, ch. 20

q: Give thyself to compunction of heart and thou shalt find devotion.
s: Book I, ch. 21

q: Thou art miserable wheresoever thou art, and whithersoever thou turnest, unless thou turn thee to God.
s: Book I, ch. 22

q: Thou knowest well how to excuse and to colour thine own deeds, but thou wilt not accept the excuses of others.
s: Book II, ch. 3

q: If thou wilt that others bear with thee, bear thou with others.
s: Book II, ch. 3

q: No good action will be distasteful to thee if thou be free within from inordinate affection.
s: Book II, ch. 4

q: There is no creature so small and vile but that it showeth us the goodness of God.
s: Book II, ch. 4

q: A pure heart seeth the very depths of heaven and hell.
s: Book II, ch. 4

q: Such as each one is inwardly, so judgeth he outwardly.
s: Book II, ch. 4

q: Little light is there within us, and what we have we quickly lose by negligence.
s: Book II, ch. 5

q: He who would weigh well and rightly his own doings would not be the man to judge severely of another.
s: Book II, ch. 5

q: Where art thou when thou art not present to thyself?
s: Book II, ch. 5

q: The testimony of a good conscience is the glory of a good man.
s: Book II, ch. 6

q: Have a good conscience and thou shalt ever have joy.
s: Book II, ch. 6

q: The glory of the good is in their conscience, and not in the report of men.
s: Book II, ch. 6

q: Thou art what thou art; and thou canst not be better than God pronounceth thee to be.
s: Book II, ch. 6

q: The love of created things is deceiving and unstable, but the love of Jesus is faithful and lasting.
s: Book II, ch. 7

q: Thou wilt find all trust little better than lost which thou hast placed in men, and not in Jesus.
s: Book II, ch. 7

s: Book II, ch. 7

q: To be without Jesus is the nethermost hell, and to be with Jesus is sweet paradise.
s: Book II, ch. 8

q: Be thou humble and peaceable and Jesus shall be with thee.
s: Book II, ch. 8

q: It is no hard thing to despise human comfort when divine is present.
s: Book II, ch. 9

q: Lord, if thou art not here, where shall I seek thee, being absent?
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: But if thou art everywhere, why do I not see thee present?
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: I have never seen thee, O Lord, my God; I do not know thy form.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Finally, I was created to see thee, and not yet have I done that for which I was made.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: He has lost the blessedness for which he was made, and has found the misery for which he was not made.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: He choked with satiety, we sigh with hunger.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Miserable exchange of how great a good, for how great an evil!
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: I strove toward God, and I stumbled on myself.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: I have come in poverty to the Rich, in misery to the Compassionate; let me not return empty and despised.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Lord, my heart is made bitter by its desolation; sweeten thou it, I beseech thee, with thy consolation.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Lord, in hunger I began to seek thee; I beseech thee that I may not cease to hunger for thee.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Lord, I am bowed down and can only look downward; raise me up that I may look upward.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: …for I cannot seek thee, except thou teach me, nor find thee, except thou reveal thyself.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: Let me seek thee in longing, let me long for thee in seeking; let me find thee in love, and love thee in finding.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: For I do not seek to understand that I may believe, but I believe in order to understand.
s: Proslogium, ch. I

q: And whatever is understood, exists in the understanding.
s: Proslogium, ch. II

q: For, it is one thing for an object to be in the understanding, and another to understand that the object exists.
s: Proslogium, ch. II

q: And indeed, we believe that thou art a being than which nothing greater can be conceived.
s: Proslogium, ch. II

q: So truly, therefore, dost thou exist, O Lord, my God, that thou canst not be conceived not to exist; and rightly.
s: Proslogium, ch. III

q: For, God is that than which a greater cannot be conceived.
s: Proslogium, ch. IV

q: For it is better to be just than not just; better to be blessed than not blessed.
s: Proslogium, ch. V

q: Truly, thou art so in terms of our experience, but thou art not so in terms of thine own.
s: Proslogium, ch. VIII

q: In this way, therefore, without contradiction thou dost justly punish and justly spare.
s: Proslogium, ch. X

q: So, then, thy compassion is born of thy justice.
s: Proslogium, ch. XI

q: For that alone is just which thou dost will; and that alone unjust which thou dost not will.
s: Proslogium, ch. XI

q: But undoubtedly, whatever thou art, thou art through nothing else than thyself.
s: Proslogium, ch. XII

q: Since, then, nothing is greater than thou, no place or time contains thee; but thou art everywhere and always.
s: Proslogium, ch. XIII

q: Why, O Lord, our God, does not my soul feel thee, if it hath found thee?
s: Proslogium, ch. XIV

q: Hence, if it has seen light and truth, it has seen thee; if it has not seen thee, it has not seen light and truth.
s: Proslogium, ch. XIV

q: Everywhere thou art wholly present, and I see thee not.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVI

q: In thee I move, and in thee I have my being; and I cannot come to thee.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVI

q: Thou art within me, and about me, and I feel thee not.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVI

q: My understanding cannot reach that light, for it shines too bright.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVI

q: Truly, I see it not, because it is too bright for me.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVI

q: For it looks, and does not see thy beauty.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVII

q: Truly, in darkness I was conceived, and in the cover of darkness I was born.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: I tried to rise to the light of God, and I have fallen back into my darkness.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: Nay, not only have I fallen into it, but I feel that I am enveloped in it.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: But everywhere thou art as a whole, and thy eternity exists as a whole forever.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: Free me from myself toward thee.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: Cleanse, heal, sharpen, enlighten the eye of my mind, that it may behold thee.
s: Proslogium, ch. XVIII

q: For nothing contains thee, but thou containest all.
s: Proslogium, ch. XIX

q: Thou art before all, and dost transcend all.
s: Proslogium, ch. XX

q: This good thou art, thou, God the Father; this is thy Word, that is, thy Son.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXIII

q: This very good is the one love common to thee and to thy Son, that is, the Holy Spirit proceeding from both.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXIII

q: For, if the created life is good, how good is the creative life!
s: Proslogium, ch. XXIV

q: Love the one good in which are all goods, and it sufficeth.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXV

q: Desire the simple good which is every good, and it is enough.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXV

q: Ask thy inmost mind whether it could contain its joy over so great a blessedness of its own.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXV

q: Doubtless they shall rejoice according as they shall love; and they shall love according as they shall know.
s: Proslogium, ch. XXVI

q: I enjoy of late more sweetness in intercession for others, than in any other part of prayer.
s: Diary, April 21, 1742

q: All I want is to be more holy, more like my dear Lord. Oh for sanctification!
s: Diary, April 25, 1742

q: O the near access that God sometimes gives us in our addresses to him!
s: Diary, April 25, 1742

q: God was so precious to me that the world, with all its enjoyments, was infinitely vile.
s: Diary, April 28, 1742

q: God gave me much power of wrestling for his cause and kingdom; and it was a happy day to my soul.
s: Diary, May 3, 1742

q: Saw so much of the wickedness of my heart that I longed to get away from myself.
s: Diary, May 13, 1742

q: O, the closest walk with God is the sweetest heaven that can be enjoyed on earth!
s: Diary, May 13, 1742

q: I never seemed to be so unhinged from myself, and to be so wholly devoted to God.
s: Diary, June 15, 1742

q: O how short do I fall of my duty in my sweetest moments!
s: Diary, June 15, 1742

q: My soul seemed to breathe after holiness, a life of constant devotedness to God.
s: Diary, June 18, 1742

q: O that the Lord would help me to hold out, yet a little while, until the happy hour of deliverance comes!
s: Diary, June 18, 1742

q: I thought that I had no power to stand for the cause of God, but was almost afraid of the shaking of a leaf.
s: Diary, June 30, 1742

q: I felt pleased to be little, to be nothing, and to lie in the dust.
s: Diary, July 4, 1742

q: We gave ourselves to God with all our hearts, to be his for ever: eternity looked very near to me while I was praying.
s: Diary, August 19, 1742

q: O, my soul tasted the sweetness of heaven; and was drawn out in prayer for the world, that it might come home to Christ!
s: Diary, August 23, 1742

q: O it is sweet to be thus weaned from friends, and from myself,…
s: Diary, October 22, 1742

q: O for holiness! O for more of God in my soul!
s: Diary, November 4, 1742

q: I feel barren and empty, as though I could not live without more of God;…
s: Diary, November 4, 1742

q: O my leanness, my barrenness, my carnality, and past bitterness, and want of a gospel temper!
s: Diary, November 27, 1742

q: May I always be willing that God should use his own methods with me!
s: Diary, December 12, 1742

q: O, how divinely sweet is it to come into the secret of his presence, and abide in his pavilion!
s: Diary, December 23, 1742

q: O, that I could spend all my time for God!
s: Diary, December 27, 1742

q: None know but those who feel it, what the soul endures that is sensibly shut out from the presence of God:…
s: Diary, January 23, 1743

q: I find my soul is more refined and weaned from a dependence on my frames and spiritual feelings.
s: Diary, February 17, 1743

q: O, that I might be serious, solemn, and always vigilant, while in an evil world!
s: Diary, February 18, 1743

q: Time appeared but an inch long, and eternity at hand;…
s: Diary, March 7, 1743

q: …and I thought I could with patience and cheerfulness bear any thing for the cause of God…
s: Diary, March 7, 1743

q: O when shall I come to that blessed world where every power of my soul will be incessantly…
s: Diary, Lord's day, March 20, 1743

q: I was greatly exercised with inward trials, and seemed to have no God to go to.
s: Diary, April 1, 1743

q: My soul was weary of my life; I longed for death, beyond measure.
s: Diary, April 7, 1743

q: Appeared to myself exceedingly ignorant, weak, helpless, unworthy, and altogether unequal to my work.
s: Diary, April 7, 1743

q: O, I longed that some dear Christian should know my distress.
s: Diary, April 16, 1743

q: O that God would enable me to live to his glory for the future!
s: Diary, April 20, 1743

q: I live in the most lonesome wilderness; have but one single person to converse with that can speak English.
s: Diary, May 18, 1743

q: I have no fellow-christian to whom I may unbosom myself, or lay open my spiritual sorrows;…
s: Diary, May 18, 1743

q: Had little or no resolution for a life of holiness; was ready almost to renounce my hope of living to God.
s: Diary, July 25, 1743

q: I longed after holiness, humility, and meekness:…
s: Diary, August 3, 1743

q: I longed that others should know how good a God the Lord is.
s: Diary, August 13, 1743

q: Yet I felt contented with my circumstances, and sweetly resigned to God.
s: Diary, August 15, 1743

q: At noon, I fell down before the Lord, groaned under my vileness, barrenness, and deadness;…
s: Diary, Lord's day, August 21, 1743

q: I poured out my soul for all the world, friends and enemies.
s: Diary, August 23, 1743

q: Eternal things engrossed all my thoughts; and I longed to be in the world of spirits.
s: Diary, August 31, 1743

q: Being sensible that I am unable to do any thing without God’s help, I do humbly entreat him, by his grace,…
s: Resolutions, preamble

q: Resolved, That I will do whatsoever I think to be most to the glory of God…
s: Resolutions, no. 1

q: Resolved, Never to do any manner of thing, whether in soul or body, less or more, but what tends to the glory of God…
s: Resolutions, no. 4

q: Resolved, Never to lose one moment of time, but to improve it in the most profitable way I possibly can.
s: Resolutions, no. 5

q: Resolved, To live with all my might, while I do live.
s: Resolutions, no. 6

q: Resolved, Never to do any thing, which I should be afraid to do if it were the last hour of my life.
s: Resolutions, no. 7

q: Resolved, To act, in all respects, both speaking and doing, as if nobody had been so vile as I…
s: Resolutions, no. 8

q: Resolved, To think much, on all occasions, of my dying, and of the common circumstances which attend death.
s: Resolutions, no. 9

q: Resolved, when I feel pain, to think of the pains of martyrdom, and of hell.
s: Resolutions, no. 10

q: Resolved, To be endeavouring to find out fit objects of liberality and charity.
s: Resolutions, no. 13

q: Resolved, Never to do any thing out of revenge.
s: Resolutions, no. 14

q: Resolved, Never to speak evil of any one, so that it shall tend to his dishonour, more or less…
s: Resolutions, no. 16

q: Resolved, That I will live so, as I shall wish I had done when I come to die.
s: Resolutions, no. 17

q: Resolved, To live so, at all times, as I think is best in my most devout frames…
s: Resolutions, no. 18

q: Resolved, To maintain the strictest temperance in eating and drinking.
s: Resolutions, no. 20

q: Resolved, Never to do any thing, which if I should see in another, I should count a just occasion to despise him for…
s: Resolutions, no. 21

q: Resolved, To endeavour to obtain for myself as much happiness in the other world as I possibly can…
s: Resolutions, no. 22

q: Resolved, Frequently to take some deliberate action, which seems most unlikely to be done, for the glory of God…
s: Resolutions, no. 23

q: Resolved, Whenever I do any conspicuously evil action, to trace it back, till I come to the original cause…
s: Resolutions, no. 24

q: Resolved, To examine carefully and constantly, what that one thing in me is, which causes me in the least to doubt of the love of God…
s: Resolutions, no. 25

q: Resolved, To cast away such things as I find do abate my assurance.
s: Resolutions, no. 26

q: Resolved, To study the Scriptures so steadily, constantly, and frequently, as that I may find…
s: Resolutions, no. 28

q: Resolved, Never to count that a prayer, nor to let that pass as a prayer, nor that as a petition of a prayer…
s: Resolutions, no. 29

q: Resolved, To strive every week to be brought higher in religion, and to a higher exercise of grace…
s: Resolutions, no. 30

q: Resolved, In narrations, never to speak any thing but the pure and simple verity.
s: Resolutions, no. 34

q: Resolved, To inquire every night, as I am going to bed, wherein I have been negligent,—what sin I have committed,—…
s: Resolutions, no. 37

q: Resolved, Never, henceforward, till I die, to act as if I were any way my own, but entirely and altogether God’s;…
s: Resolutions, no. 43

q: Resolved, Never to give over, nor in the least to slacken, my fight with my corruptions, however unsuccessful I may be.
s: Resolutions, no. 56

q: Resolved, After afflictions, to inquire, what I am the better for them; what good I have got by them;…
s: Resolutions, no. 67

q: Let there be something of benevolence in all that I speak.
s: Resolutions, no. 70

q: I made seeking my salvation the main business of my life.

s: Personal Narrative

q: Pure and humble, holy and heavenly, Christianity appeared exceedingly amiable to me.
s: Personal Narrative

q: The heaven I desired was a heaven of holiness;…
s: Personal Narrative

s: Personal Narrative

q: God’s excellency, his wisdom, his purity, and love, seemed to appear in every thing;…
s: Personal Narrative

s: Personal Narrative

q: I had vehement longings of soul after God and Christ, and after more holiness,…
